## Treatment coding for Hogwarts houses

We used House to predict Machiavellianism, with $k-1 = 3$ dummy variables.

| House | Hufflepuff | Ravenclaw | Slytherin | Predicted value |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|---:|
| Gryffindor | 0 | 0 | 0 | $a$ |
| Hufflepuff | 1 | 0 | 0 | $a+b_1$ |
| Ravenclaw | 0 | 1 | 0 | $a+b_2$ |
| Slytherin | 0 | 0 | 1 | $a+b_3$ |

. . .

The intercept $a$ is Gryffindor's mean. Each slope is a house mean minus Gryffindor's mean.

## Testing house differences

| Question | Test | SPSS table |
|---|---|---|
| Does Slytherin differ from Gryffindor? | $t$-test for $b_3$ | Coefficients |
| Are all four population means equal? | Overall $F$-test | ANOVA |

. . .

The overall $F$-test compares between-house and within-house mean squares, with $k-1$ and $N-k$ degrees of freedom.

For Hogwarts, $F(3,843)=36.26$ and $p<.001$. House explains $11.4\%$ of the observed variation in Machiavellianism ($\eta^2=R^2=.114$).
